story_title: As the assigned Event Coordinator, I want each venue booked for an event to be checked against what that particular space is needed for so that a breakout room is not judged by the whole event's attendance and the event is only confirmed when every room is secured

acceptance_criteria.text: For each venue booking request, the Coordinator records what the space is for (e.g. main programme, breakout room) and the expected attendance and room layout for that space.
Given the event has only one venue booking, when the request is made, then the space's expected attendance and layout default to the event's own.
Each venue's suitability is checked independently, against the attendance, layout, accessibility and facilities recorded for that space rather than the event's total expected attendance.
Given a venue is unsuitable for its space, when the check runs, then the unmet requirement is identified for that booking only and the event's other bookings are not affected.
The purpose of each space is shown with its booking wherever the event's venue bookings are listed, including to Venue Staff reviewing the request.

Given an event has more than one venue booking, when the Coordinator attempts to confirm the event, then every required venue booking must be confirmed; otherwise confirmation is refused and the unconfirmed booking is identified.
An event with a single venue booking is checked and confirmed as it is today.

open_questions: Written 2026-10-13, before any SPM-90 code (test-first), then checked against the built screens the same day: no wording in the cases had to change. Checked against Week 7 Customer Changes (Change #3), docs/CUSTOMER_CLARIFICATIONS.md, SPM-81's cases and open questions, and the code on this branch. All 11 cases passed when run by hand on 2026-10-13 (kayalvizhi24), with the migration applied and `npm run fixtures:spm90` loaded. The browser writes September as 'Sept' where the cases say 'Sep'; that is the browser's date format and counts as a match. SPM-90-TC02, TC04 and TC05 were reworded during the pass to open their event first. Every 'DECIDED' entry below is wording or behaviour chosen here, not in the story.

RESOLVED 2026-10-13 (AC3, decided by kayalvizhi24): facilities and accessibility requirements stay the event's and apply to every space it books; only attendance and layout are the space's own. AC3 mentions the 'accessibility and facilities recorded for that space', but AC1 has the Coordinator record only the purpose, attendance and layout, and the estimate sizes the story as 'a small migration for purpose and attendance per booking'. Week 7 Change #3, the Week 1 and Week 4 briefings, the discussion board and CUSTOMER_CLARIFICATIONS.md were checked: none asks for facilities per room, and sessions already work this way (UI_DESIGN.md: 'Facilities, accessibility needs and registration stay event-wide'). So a breakout room must still have the event's mandatory 'Step-free access' (SPM-90-TC02). Per-room facility lists would be a new, larger story touching SPM-39, SPM-40 and SPM-62.

FINDING (AC6): confirmation is already refused while any listed venue booking is pending. Track Outstanding Arrangements (SPM-33, merged after SPM-81) lists each pending or approved booking as its own arrangement, and Confirm refuses on every required one that is not approved (src/lib/eventConfirmation.ts; SPM-33-TC01). The Known Gap 'An event with more than one venue can be confirmed while one is still pending' in DOCUMENTATION.md is out of date and is removed with this story. What SPM-90 adds for AC6 is the space's purpose in the refusal and on the Readiness tab, so the unconfirmed booking is identified by what it is for (SPM-90-TC08).

RESOLVED 2026-10-13 (AC6, 'required'): a venue booking the Coordinator has marked as not required does not stop confirmation. That is SPM-33's rule and is covered by its cases, so no case here repeats it. A rejected, withdrawn or released request is not a booking and never blocks.

DECIDED 2026-10-13 (AC1, AC3, where the space is recorded): the Venue tab gets a card 'The space you need' with 'Expected attendance for this space' (number), 'Room layout' (the same layout list as the event form, plus 'Not set') and a 'Check venues' button. The venue list is judged against those two values and the event's facilities. Without this, a breakout room would be 'Not suitable' for the event's attendance and would have no 'Request booking' button at all. 'Request booking' carries the two values to the request form.

DECIDED 2026-10-13 (AC1, the request form): 'Request a venue booking' gets three fields above 'Date': 'What is this space for?' (text, required, up to 100 characters, hint 'For example main programme or breakout room.'), 'Expected attendance for this space' (whole number, at least 1, required) and 'Room layout'. The read-only 'Layout' row in the summary above the form is removed. Messages: 'Say what this space is for.' and 'Enter a whole number of at least 1.', each under its field.

DECIDED 2026-10-13 (AC2, defaults): attendance and layout start on the event's own (the session's own, for a multi-session event) for every request; the Coordinator changes them for a smaller space. 'What is this space for?' starts as 'Main programme' when the event (or that session) has no pending or approved booking yet, and empty otherwise, so a second room has to be named. Choosing another session on the Venue tab resets 'The space you need' to that session's values.

DECIDED 2026-10-13 (AC3, AC4 wording): the capacity line changes from '… - your event expects N.' to '… - this space expects N.', and the refusal from '<venue> is not suitable for this event: …' to '<venue> is not suitable for this space: …', because the figure is no longer always the event's. The Venue tab's subtitle becomes 'Each venue is checked against the attendance and layout of the space you need, and this event's facilities and accessibility needs.' One case of another story quotes the old wording and is listed in DOCUMENTATION.md Known Gaps: SPM-42-TC02.

DECIDED 2026-10-13 (AC5, where the purpose is shown): (1) the Venue tab's 'Booking requests' card, as '<purpose> · <session> · <date and times> · <layout> · <N> attendees'; (2) Venue Staff's 'Booking Requests' page, as a 'Space' row, with 'Expected attendance' now the space's own figure; (3) the Overview's 'Venue bookings' card, as '<room> (<code>) · <purpose> · <layout> · seats <n>'; (4) the Readiness tab, as 'Space: <purpose>' before 'Booking status', and in the outstanding reason as '<room> (<purpose>) for this event …'. The one-line 'Venue' summary rows (Overview, organiser's glance) still name rooms only.

DECIDED 2026-10-13 (bookings made before this story): the migration adds two nullable columns to venue_bookings, purpose and expected_attendance. It fills expected_attendance for existing bookings from their session's or event's attendance (what they were checked against) and leaves purpose empty. A booking with no purpose shows no purpose segment (Venue tab, Overview, Readiness) and 'Not recorded' in Venue Staff's 'Space' row. Covered by SPM-90-TC10.

DECIDED 2026-10-13 (limits not in the story): a space's attendance is not capped by the event's expected attendance, and the spaces' attendances are not added up or compared with the event's total. The story asks for neither.

DECIDED 2026-10-13 (venue changes, SPM-39): when Venue Staff edit or retire a venue, a booking is re-checked against its own space's attendance (falling back to the session's or event's for a booking without one), so a 20-person breakout room is not flagged because the room no longer seats the whole event. No manual case here: it is SPM-39's screen, covered by automated tests.

RESOLVED 2026-10-13 (out of scope): 'Search with filters' (Find a venue, SPM-40) still filters by the event's own requirements; its 'Request booking' opens the form on the event's defaults, which the Coordinator can change there. Submit for safety check (SPM-86) uses the same arrangements rule as Confirm and is not re-tested here.

For the team, still open from SPM-81: the equipment availability check works out transfer time from 'the event's venue' and picks one booking (venueFor() in src/lib/equipmentAvailabilityService.ts). Recording what each space is for does not by itself say which room the equipment goes to. Not changed by this story unless the team decides a rule (for example: the 'Main programme' space, or the largest).
